ic_name: ARM Serial Wire Debug (SWD) — ADIv5 (ARM IHI 0031C)
power_on_sequence: 1. Power-up: SWD wire-level state may be indeterminate.
2. Host drives ≥ 50 SWCLK cycles with SWDIO=HIGH (line reset); SW-DP unconditionally returns to Idle, SELECT and CTRL/STAT clear, posted-read queue drained.
3. Host issues an IDCODE/DPIDR read: Request(APnDP=0, RnW=1, A[2:3]=0); target responds ACK=OK + 32-bit DPIDR + parity; host validates DPIDR.RAO bit 0 = 1.
4. Host requests system + debug power-up: writes CTRL/STAT with CSYSPWRUPREQ=1 + CDBGPWRUPREQ=1; reads CTRL/STAT and waits for CSYSPWRUPACK=1 + CDBGPWRUPACK=1.
5. Host clears any sticky errors from boot: writes ABORT with STKERRCLR=STKCMPCLR=ORUNERRCLR=WDERRCLR=1.
6. Host walks the AP IDR catalog: for APSEL=0..255, writes SELECT.APSEL=N then reads AP[N].IDR (offset 0xFC); a non-zero IDR identifies a present AP.
swj_dp_mode_switch_sequence_jtag_to_swd: 1. Start in JTAG mode (SWJ-DP) — TMS/TCK/TDI/TDO pads active as JTAG.
2. Drive ≥ 50 SWCLK (=TCK) cycles with TMS=1 — JTAG TAP unconditionally reaches TestLogicReset; SWJ-DP wakes the SWD-select watcher.
3. Shift the 16-bit JTAG-to-SWD selection sequence 0xE79E LSB-first on TMS, synchronous to TCK rising edges.
4. Drive ≥ 50 SWCLK cycles with TMS (=SWDIO) = 1 — performs an SWD line reset in the new mode.
5. Issue an SWD IDCODE/DPIDR read transaction; verify ACK=OK + valid DPIDR; SWJ-DP is now in SWD mode.
swj_dp_mode_switch_sequence_swd_to_jtag: 2. Drive ≥ 50 SWCLK cycles with SWDIO=1 — SWD line reset; SWJ-DP wakes the JTAG-select watcher.
3. Shift the 16-bit SWD-to-JTAG selection sequence 0xE73C LSB-first on SWDIO (=TMS), synchronous to SWCLK rising edges.
4. Drive ≥ 50 SWCLK (=TCK) cycles with TMS=1 — JTAG TAP unconditionally reaches TestLogicReset.
5. Issue a JTAG IR-scan to load BYPASS/IDCODE and verify the JTAG TAP responds; SWJ-DP is now in JTAG mode.
ap_read_sequence_posted: 1. Host writes SELECT with target AP index + AP bank for the desired AP register.
2. Host issues Read AP[N] register X — Request(APnDP=1, RnW=1, A[2:3]=X).
3. Target responds ACK=OK + 32-bit data + parity. NOTE: the data field is implementation-defined for the first read of a sequence (typically zero or a stale buffer).
4. Host issues Read AP[N] register Y (or DP.RDBUFF) — Request(APnDP=1, RnW=1, A[2:3]=Y).
5. Target responds ACK=OK + 32-bit data + parity; this data is the ACTUAL result of step 2's read.
6. To recover the last read in a burst, host reads DP.RDBUFF (APnDP=0, RnW=1, A[2:3]=0xC); the data field returns the most recent posted-read result.
ap_write_sequence: 1. Host writes SELECT with target AP index + AP bank.
2. Host issues Write AP[N] register X — Request(APnDP=1, RnW=0, A[2:3]=X) + 32-bit data + parity.
3. Target responds ACK=OK (or WAIT if busy; FAULT if sticky error).
4. Host's next transaction may proceed; the write may still be in flight on the system bus (TrInProg bit in CSW indicates completion).
mem_ap_memory_write_burst_sequence: 1. Host configures CSW: AddrInc=Single (or Packed), Size=Word (010), DbgSwEnable=1.
2. Host writes TAR with the starting system-bus address.
3. Host issues N successive Write DRW transactions, each carrying a 32-bit word; target auto-increments TAR by 4 per transfer (Single mode) and writes each word to the system bus.
4. Host issues a final RDBUFF read to flush any in-flight transaction; OK acknowledges the burst is complete.
5. (Optional) Host issues a Memory Barrier Transfer (MBT) write to flush system-bus write buffers if the AP supports it.
mem_ap_memory_read_burst_sequence: 2. Host writes TAR with the starting system-bus address.
3. Host issues N successive Read DRW transactions; each transaction reads the previous DRW's result; TAR auto-increments by 4 per transfer.
4. Host issues a final DP.RDBUFF read to recover the data of the last DRW read.
5. The N reads + 1 RDBUFF cover N words; host slices the SWDIO stream per-transaction.
fault_recovery_sequence: 1. Target returns ACK=FAULT (100) on a transaction.
2. Host issues Read DP.CTRL/STAT to read the sticky-error bits; identifies STICKYORUN / STICKYCMP / STICKYERR / WDATAERR.
3. Host issues Write DP.ABORT with the corresponding clear bits (ORUNERRCLR / STKCMPCLR / STKERRCLR / WDERRCLR + DAPABORT if a long AP transaction was in flight).
4. Host re-reads DP.CTRL/STAT to confirm the sticky bits are clear.
5. Host retries the failed transaction; if WAIT persists, host backs off SWCLK frequency or retries with longer Turnaround.
wait_recovery_sequence: 1. Target returns ACK=WAIT (010); the data field is meaningless.
2. Host advances 1 or more SWCLK cycles (idle) and retries the same Request.
3. Repeat until ACK=OK or until host gives up and performs a line reset / debug-reset request.
swd_line_reset_recovery_sequence: 1. Host detects a protocol error (invalid ACK pattern, parity mismatch, stuck bus).
2. Host drives SWDIO=HIGH for ≥ 50 consecutive SWCLK cycles; SW-DP wire-level FSM returns to Idle.
3. Host re-issues IDCODE/DPIDR read; verifies ACK=OK + valid DPIDR.
4. Host re-writes SELECT (the line reset cleared it) before the next AP transaction.
5. Host re-clears any sticky bits via ABORT (the line reset cleared CTRL/STAT).
multidrop_target_selection_sequence_adiv: 1. Host drives ≥ 50 SWCLK cycles with SWDIO=HIGH (line reset).
2. Host shifts the JTAG-to-SWD 16-bit selection sequence 0xE79E LSB-first (puts all SWJ-DPs in SWD mode if applicable).
3. Host drives another ≥ 50 SWCLK cycles with SWDIO=HIGH (line reset, this time in SWD mode).
4. Host issues Write DP.TARGETSEL with the desired target's TPARTNO + TINSTANCE value.
5. Only the matching target drives ACK on subsequent transactions; all other targets ignore the bus.
6. Host issues Read DP.DPIDR to confirm the addressed target responds correctly.
7. To switch to a different target, repeat steps 1-6 with the new target's TPARTNO + TINSTANCE.
cortex_m_halt_sequence_via_swd: 1. Power-on sequence + IDCODE + power-up requests (per power_on_sequence above).
2. Host walks the MEM-AP.BASE → CoreSight ROM Table to locate the Cortex-M CPU debug-register block (DHCSR / DCRSR / DCRDR / DEMCR / FPB / DWT base addresses).
3. Host configures MEM-AP: CSW.Size=Word, CSW.AddrInc=Off, CSW.DbgSwEnable=1.
4. Host writes TAR = DHCSR address; writes DRW = (DBGKEY=0xA05F << 16) | (C_DEBUGEN=1) | (C_HALT=1).
5. Target halts; host reads DHCSR via DRW (with RDBUFF flush) and verifies S_HALT=1.
6. Host may then access CPU registers via DCRSR + DCRDR, or memory via TAR + DRW.
tap_recovery_sequence: Drive SWDIO=HIGH for ≥ 50 consecutive SWCLK cycles → SW-DP line reset regardless of current state.
If SWJ-DP and stuck in JTAG mode: drive TMS=1 for ≥ 5 TCKs → JTAG TestLogicReset; then perform JTAG-to-SWD selection sequence 0xE79E; then SWD line reset.
(Optional) Some SoCs implement an nTRST pad: assert nTRST=LOW for the spec's minimum pulse width → SWJ-DP forced to power-on default state.
